{"id":"COR-2279","uuid":"6189169f-679e-4244-ab50-c24a7623ef3c","title":"brain: hosted facts sync retries 403 forever on a stale repo binding (deleted repo / lost access) — trips brainstore auth-failure monitor","description":"## What happened

`[brainstore eks-prod-us-east-2] auth failures (401/403)` fired at 2026-10-27 07:00 UTC (P2 via [incident.io](<http://incident.io>), [alert thread](<https://entireio.slack.com/archives/C0B1Y3Y6PFD/p1793084472753739>)). It was 11 × **403** `no repo grant` in 10 min, 0 × 401, all on `/brain/facts` (`facts_get` / `facts_upsert`), from 3 callers. One CLI's session-end burst was 7 of the 11.

Brainstore is behaving correctly: core denies pull for these callers. The bug is client-side. The repo binding written by `entire brain connect` never refreshes, so once the bound repo is deleted or the caller loses access, every trigger keeps retrying the same 403.

The 403s on `/brain/memories*` from the public-repo read gap are already fixed. That fix (brainstore `2a56abf`) has been live since 01:23 UTC, with 0 memories 403s since. Before it there were 70 in 31h. All remaining 403s are CLI facts sync.

## The 4 stuck bindings (us-east-2, last 24h, 66 × 403)

| Repo | Placement (entire MCP `cell_repo_placement`) | Pattern | Cause |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `01M5TTVWKNZ3QQHNBMJQR5CTHC` | 404 in US cell | 403 throughout | **Deleted.** entire-backup logged `reconcile drift → tombstone — repo deleted` at 06:01 |
| `01M5XED6V2RQBDSDJVME00SQH0` | 404 in US cell | 200 until 02:08, 403 from 02:18 | Most likely deleted (no tombstone seen) |
| `01M5XB979X8WY3VN5XWHSNKFRA` | GitHub mirror `TradeForm/TradeForm`, placement `cached_at` 06:50:08 | 51 × 200 from 02:05–06:43, 403 from 06:52 | Repo exists; caller lost pull at \~06:50. Placement cache refreshed in that same window. **Cause unknown** |
| `01M5R70ESVFW10Q15W4V2KJNYF` | Entire-native repo, owned by a different account's project | 403 throughout | Repo exists; caller has no grant. **Cause unknown** |

### Callers per repo

One caller per repo, all in eks-prod-us-east-2. Identity logging started \~01:23 UTC 2026-10-27, so earlier 403s are unattributed (7-day total: 275 × 403).

| Repo | Handle | Account ID | Issuer | 403s (UTC, 2026-10-27) |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `01M5TTVWKNZ3QQHNBMJQR5CTHC` | awfixer | `01KXATRWZS28QPWBQZ0WNDF9SQ` | us.auth | 18, 01:31 → 05:25 |
| `01M5XED6V2RQBDSDJVME00SQH0` | EsTharian | `01M5XE8J6EBJA7DD4PFV0WCA3R` | sg.auth | 22, 02:18 → 06:49 |
| `01M5XB979X8WY3VN5XWHSNKFRA` | Kedaar-NR | `01M5XAEGM9EHT7G4FAV492JR3M` | us.auth | 20, 06:52 → 07:17 (ongoing) |
| `01M5R70ESVFW10Q15W4V2KJNYF` | ColeDriver | `01KS9X4TZYP31RXT1K90CB6PHK` | us.auth | 21, 01:43 → 07:13 (ongoing) |

Placement IDs for the grant audit (from `cell_repo_placement`):

* `TradeForm/TradeForm` (`01M5XB979X8WY3VN5XWHSNKFRA`): repo group `01M5XB98K0VQX4GNDGTCFS1N4Z`, owning project `01M5XAKKE8B8WHTY9MXZ4BK07P`
* `poopiecatoure/fartknuckle` (`01M5R70ESVFW10Q15W4V2KJNYF`): owning project `01M5R70DV45ASV2C26PF2VARHR`

Datadog has no logs from other services (core, mirror pipeline) for these repo, project, or repo-group IDs, or for the callers, in the flip windows. Why access changed has to come from core/SpiceDB audit.

## Why the client hammers

* `factsync.UpsertFacts` / `FactsFeedPage` turn 403 into a generic "unexpected status" error (`internal/factsync/perfact.go:82`, `:124`). `hostedFactsSyncAndPull` never fails, so it logs to stderr and moves on.
* The session-end hook is not throttled: 2 branches × (POST + GET) = **4 requests per session end**, all answered 403 with the same token (`internal/cli/hook_cmd.go:157`).
* The daemon tick (15 min × 2 branches) and the push hint (≤1/min) also retry indefinitely.
* Brainstore maps core 404 → 403 on purpose (anti-enumeration), so the client can't tell "deleted" from "no access".

### Push vs pull on a stale binding

* `pushHostedFacts` (`internal/cli/hosted_sync.go:131`) re-uploads the **whole** branch store on every trigger, in 1,000-record chunks. The upsert is idempotent, so this is by design. An empty store returns early and sends nothing (`:136`). On a 403 it stops at the first chunk, logs `publish failed… pull-only`, then runs the pull, which also gets a 403.
* Observed: only Kedaar-NR POSTs (`facts_upsert` 403s), on every session end for both branches. ColeDriver, EsTharian, and awfixer have empty local stores, so they only GET.
* Local facts are safe. A failed push doesn't touch the store, and a failed pull returns before the branch-store rebuild (`:103`). Facts just never reach the server.
* Side effect of full-store upload: even on healthy repos every session end POSTs the entire store. That's acceptable at current sizes, but stopping on 403 also stops a stuck client from re-sending its whole store every time.

## Proposed fix (entire-brain, \~80 lines + tests)

1. `factsync`: add a sentinel `ErrNoAccess`, returned on 403 by both calls.
2. On `ErrNoAccess`, end the run: skip the pull and the remaining branches.
3. Re-resolve placement (`entire repo view --json`). If origin now resolves to a **different** repo id (deleted and re-onboarded), rebind and continue.
4. Otherwise store `no access until now+24h` next to the binding. Session-end, daemon, and push-hint sync skip the repo while it's set; `entire brain connect` clears it. Print one actionable line: "no access to this repo on Entire; run `entire brain connect` once access is granted".

401 and 404 (not-in-region) keep their current behavior, since those should keep reaching the monitor.

## Monitor follow-up (separate, brainstore)

The monitor sums raw requests (`sum:brainstore.http.responses{auth_failure:true}` > 10 / 10m), so one looping client can trip it alone. It was built to catch systemic breaks (JWKS/issuer drift, a core grants regression, misrouting), which affect many callers at once. Consider a rejection *rate*, or a log-based monitor on distinct `@account_id`. The `account_id` / `deny_reason` fields are available since brainstore `477b247`.

1	package cli
2	
3	import (
4		"bytes"
5		"context"
6		"errors"
7		"fmt"
8		"io"
9		"sort"
10		"strings"
11	
12		"github.com/entireio/entire-brain/factmerge"
13		"github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/apiurl"
14		"github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/cli/internal/base"
15		"github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/cli/internal/brainstore"
16		"github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/cli/internal/factstore"
17		"github.com/entireio/entire-brain/internal/factsync"
18	)
19	
20	const (
21		// hostedUpsertChunk stays well under brainstore's 5000-record batch cap
22		// and its 32 MiB body cap.
23		hostedUpsertChunk = 1000
24		// hostedFeedPageSize is brainstore's page-size ceiling.
25		hostedFeedPageSize = 100
26		// maxHostedFeedPages bounds one pull so the never-fails path cannot spin
27		// on a pathological feed. ponytail: a delta larger than 20k records
28		// finishes on the next trigger — the cursor persists either way.
29		maxHostedFeedPages = 200
30	)
31	
32	// hostedSyncOutcome reports what one hostedFactsSyncAndPull run did.
33	type hostedSyncOutcome struct {
34		Attempted     bool
35		PullSucceeded bool
36	}
37	
38	// hostedFactsSyncAndPull closes the hosted-memory loop for one branch on the
39	// per-fact wire (COR-2126): batch-upsert this machine's branch store to
40	// brainstore, pull the repo-wide delta feed into the repo-level cache, and
41	// rebuild the branch store as the pull filter's output plus this machine's
42	// own facts the feed has not seen. No CAS, no branch heads, no proposals —
43	// per-fact storage keeps conflicting facts side by side and resolution stays
44	// deferred to the async pipeline.
45	//
46	// It is a NEVER-FAILS step: every gated or soft failure is one stderr line and
47	// a nil return, because its callers (daemon tick, session-end hook, connect)
48	// must not fail on hosted outages. The error return exists for programming
49	// errors only.
50	//
51	// Gate order is fixed: (1) the local-only kill switch always wins; (2) a
52	// recorded opt-out (`entire brain disconnect`) stops sync until `connect`
53	// clears it; (3) the repo binding is the consent AND the connection state —
54	// only `entire brain connect` (or the future onboarding flow) writes it, so an
55	// absent binding means local-only, silently, every run. Background triggers
56	// never connect a repo. (4) apiurl.Validate before any client exists. A fresh
57	// token is minted per call via the host CLI's own login and held only in
58	// memory.
59	//
60	// The outcome reports what actually happened: Attempted is whether the gates
61	// passed and the server was contacted (callers that log success must not
62	// report a gated no-op as a sync that ran); PullSucceeded is whether the pull
63	// half completed — the half that proves the exchange (the per-branch marker
64	// keys off it). Callers that promise a sync to the user (connect) key their
65	// report off PullSucceeded; background callers keep ignoring it.
66	func hostedFactsSyncAndPull(ctx context.Context, errW io.Writer, opts Options, repoDir string, storage repoStorage, branch string) (hostedSyncOutcome, error) {
67		if base.BrainNoEgressMode() {
68			return hostedSyncOutcome{}, nil
69		}
70		binding, present, err := brainstore.ReadHostedRepoBinding(storage.BrainDir)
71		if err != nil {
72			// NO unreadable binding may fall through to auto-connect: the file may
73			// hide a recorded opt-out (privacy) or a custom target, and neither
74			// survives a rewrite. Skip loudly; the remedy is an explicit

251			// Same fail-closed rule as the old head pull: a record whose content id
252			// does not re-derive is a forgery, and nothing from this feed — cache
253			// and cursor included — may land until the server stops serving it.
254			if err := factmerge.VerifyIdentities(keptRecords); err != nil {
255				return fmt.Errorf("refused untrustworthy feed: %w", err)
256			}
257			sort.Slice(keptRecords, func(i, j int) bool { return keptRecords[i].ID < keptRecords[j].ID })
258	
259			if err := writeHostedFeedCache(feedDir, hostedFeedState{RepoID: repoID, BaseURL: baseURL, Cursor: cursor}, items); err != nil {
260				return err
261			}
262	
263			existing, err := factstore.Load(storage.BrainDir, branch)
264			if err != nil {
265				return err
266			}
267			for _, fact := range keptRecords {
268				// upsertFact never moves a local status, so a locally retracted
269				// fact stays retracted whatever the feed says. The feed is
270				// authoritative for RETIREMENTS, though: lifecycle moves one way —
271				// active to retired, never a revival.
272				existing = upsertFact(existing, fact)
273				if fact.Status == factStatusActive {
274					continue
275				}
276				if i := indexOfFact(existing, fact.ID); i >= 0 && existing[i].Status == factStatusActive {
277					existing[i].Status = fact.Status
278					existing[i].SupersededBy = fact.SupersededBy
279					existing[i].UpdatedAt = opts.Now().UTC()
280				}
281			}
282			// The branch store is the filter output plus this machine's own facts
283			// the feed has not seen (unsynced or push-denied). A record the feed
284			// knows but the filter rejected is another branch's — or a recycled
285			// name's — fact: drop it. This is what replaces rename/recycle
286			// detection (lineage.json is cancelled). Three stand-downs guard
287			// against evicting this machine's own knowledge when the feed's copy
288			// fails the filter (first-writer attribution can belong to a teammate
289			// who pushed the same statement first, carrying only THEIR anchors):
290			// a transcript anchor is proof the fact was distilled here
291			// (SanitizeForEgress strips it on push, so a pulled copy never
292			// carries one); the local copy's OWN anchors get the same keep filter
293			// (judged memberless — being in this store is not proof of
294			// authorship), so a locally reachable commit or an anchor-less pool
295			// fact survives; and with no member identity the filter cannot
296			// recognize this member's facts at all, so removal is disabled
297			// rather than evicting them wholesale.
298			rebuilt := existing[:0]
299			for _, rec := range existing {
300				if _, inFeed := items[rec.ID]; member != "" && inFeed && !keptIDs[rec.ID] &&
301					!hasLocalProvenance(rec) && !keepHostedFact(factsync.FeedItem{Record: rec}, "", reachable) {
302					continue
303				}
304				rebuilt = append(rebuilt, rec)
305			}
306			if err := factstore.Write(storage.BrainDir, branch, rebuilt); err != nil {
307				return err
308			}
309			// A manifest failure reports alongside the successful pull instead of
310			// masking it.
311			manifestErr = updateFactSourceManifestLocked(storage.BrainDir, opts.Now().UTC())
312			kept, total = len(keptRecords), len(items)
313			return nil
314		})
315		return kept, total, manifestErr, err
316	}
317	
318	// hostedSyncBranch resolves the branch a hosted sync step should cover: the
319	// repo's current branch, else the default branch.
320	func hostedSyncBranch(ctx context.Context, runner CommandRunner, repoDir string) string {
321		if current, err := base.GitScalar(ctx, runner, repoDir, "branch", "--show-current"); err == nil {
322			if branch := strings.TrimSpace(current); branch != "" {
323				return branch
324			}
325		}
326		return distillDefaultBranch
327	}

11	// HostedRepoBinding is the repo-level hosted-brain connection state, written
12	// by `entire brain connect` and `entire brain disconnect`. Only non-secrets
13	// live here; tokens are minted per call (see mintHostedToken). The per-branch
14	// hosted-target.json (hostedFactsBinding) records which branches have synced.
15	//
16	// OptedOut records an explicit `disconnect`: no sync until
17	// `connect` rewrites the binding. The coordinates are kept through an opt-out
18	// so re-connecting works without placement resolution. Disconnect never purges
19	// memories already pulled into the local store.
20	type HostedRepoBinding struct {
21		RepoID   string `json:"repo_id"`
22		BaseURL  string `json:"base_url"`
23		OptedOut bool   `json:"opted_out,omitempty"`
24	}
25	
26	const HostedRepoBindingFile = "hosted.json"
27	
28	func WriteHostedRepoBinding(brainDir string, binding HostedRepoBinding) error {
29		return WithBrainWriteLock(brainDir, func() error {
30			return writeHostedRepoBindingLocked(brainDir, binding)
31		})
32	}
33	
34	// writeHostedRepoBindingLocked is the write half for callers that already hold
35	// the brain write lock (it is not reentrant).
36	func writeHostedRepoBindingLocked(brainDir string, binding HostedRepoBinding) error {
37		binding.BaseURL = strings.TrimRight(binding.BaseURL, "/")
38		data, err := json.Marshal(binding)
39		if err != nil {
40			return err
41		}
42		return WriteBrainRelativeFileAtomic(brainDir, HostedRepoBindingFile, append(data, '\n'), 0600)
43	}
44	
45	// SetHostedOptOut records an explicit disconnect as one locked
46	// read-modify-write, so a concurrent writer cannot interleave between reading
47	// the coordinates and marking them opted out. A corrupt state file must not
48	// block the opt-out — the user's intent is unambiguous — so it is replaced by
49	// a bare one. Returns the binding as written.
50	func SetHostedOptOut(brainDir string) (HostedRepoBinding, error) {
51		var binding HostedRepoBinding
52		err := WithBrainWriteLock(brainDir, func() error {
53			existing, _, readErr := ReadHostedRepoBinding(brainDir)
54			if readErr != nil {
55				existing = HostedRepoBinding{}
56			}
57			existing.OptedOut = true
58			binding = existing
59			return writeHostedRepoBindingLocked(brainDir, existing)
60		})
61		return binding, err
62	}
63	
64	func ReadHostedRepoBinding(brainDir string) (HostedRepoBinding, bool, error) {
65		var binding HostedRepoBinding
66		data, present, err := ReadMemoryStateFile(brainDir, HostedRepoBindingFile, "hosted repo binding", base.DefaultMaxReadBytes)
67		if err != nil || !present {
68			return binding, false, err
69		}
70		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &binding); err != nil {
71			return binding, false, fmt.Errorf("invalid hosted repo binding: %w", err)
72		}
73		binding.BaseURL = strings.TrimRight(binding.BaseURL, "/")
74		return binding, true, nil
75	}

I'm designing the error handling: adding an ErrNoAccess sentinel in factsync for 403 responses from UpsertFacts and FactsFeedPage, then making hostedFactsSyncAndPull skip the pull step when push hits that error—while also ensuring callers that loop over branches stop processing remaining ones.

Rather than writing a NoAccess flag into Outcome, I'm thinking it's simpler to persist a no-access marker when the error occurs, so subsequent branch calls in the same loop read the binding, see the marker, and skip automatically without touching every call site. For re-resolving placement, I'm planning to shell out to repo view when access is denied—if it resolves to a different repo ID, rebind and retry once; otherwise write a no-access-until timestamp.

I'm also checking the import structure—resolveHostedPlacement lives in the connect command package, and I need to confirm hostedFactsSyncAndPull in the cli package can actually import it, which it seems it can since connect_config.go already does.

Since resolveHostedPlacement is unexported, I need to either export it from connect or duplicate the logic; exporting it is cleaner given cli already imports connect in that direction. For storing the no-access marker, I'm considering adding a NoAccessUntil field directly to the hosted binding file, since rebinding naturally overwrites the whole file and clears the marker automatically—a tidy side effect.

The sync paths just need to check this field and skip silently while it's set in the future, and the issue clarifies the three gating points and that connect clears it. To avoid races and respect the rule that hosted.json should never be rewritten blindly, I should implement the write as a locked read-modify-write similar to SetHostedOptOut, so a concurrent disconnect can't be clobbered and existing fields like OptedOut stay preserved.

Rebinding on re-resolve needs the same careful treatment — it should re-verify under the lock that OptedOut hasn't flipped and that the stale RepoID still matches before committing the new binding, since WriteHostedRepoBinding takes its own lock rather than being reentrant.

For ErrNoAccess specifically, I'm planning to skip the pull if push fails that way, and route both push and pull access errors through a shared handleNoAccess handler that attempts the rebind.

After attempting rebind, if the resolved repoID differs from the current binding and is non-empty, I'll recheck the binding is unchanged and not opted out, then return the new binding to retry once; otherwise I'll set a 24-hour no-access cooldown and print a single actionable line about syncing being paused. I'll make the no-access skip silent, consistent with how opt-out is handled, rather than printing a line on every trigger — but I should surface this state in `entire brain status` for visibility, since its gate order mirrors this one. 19	// subtract.

30	}
31	
32	const (
33		hostedStateConnected    = "connected"
34		hostedStateLocalOnly    = "local_only"
35		hostedStateDisconnected = "disconnected"
36	)
37

39	// gate order as hostedFactsSyncAndPull: the kill switch wins, then the binding
40	// decides. The binding stays visible under the kill switch so the reader sees
41	// what it suppresses. A corrupt binding degrades to disconnected with a warning
42	// rather than failing status over a sync-state file.
43	func buildHostedStatus(brainDir string, factBranches []string) (*brainStatusHosted, string) {
44		var warning string
45		hosted := &brainStatusHosted{RepoState: hostedStateDisconnected}
46		binding, present, err := brainstore.ReadHostedRepoBinding(brainDir)
47		switch {
48		case err != nil:
49			warning = "hosted binding unreadable (run '" + base.BrainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, "connect") + "' to rebind): " + err.Error()
50		case present && binding.OptedOut:
51			// Coordinates survive an opt-out (reconnect needs no placement
52			// resolution), so the target stays visible here too.
53			hosted.RepoID = binding.RepoID
54			hosted.BaseURL = binding.BaseURL
55		case present:
56			hosted.RepoState = hostedStateConnected
57			hosted.RepoID = binding.RepoID
58			hosted.BaseURL = binding.BaseURL
59			// A broken marker is corruption, not "never synced" — report it like
60			// the unreadable top-level binding above instead of posing as a
61			// healthy unsynced branch. The two warnings cannot co-occur: markers
62			// are only inspected when the binding itself was readable.
63			var broken []string
64			var brokenErr error
65			for _, branch := range factBranches {
66				marker, markerPresent, markerErr := readHostedFactsBinding(brainDir, branch)
67				switch {
68				case markerErr != nil:
69					broken = append(broken, branch)
70					if brokenErr == nil {
71						brokenErr = markerErr
72					}
73				case markerPresent && marker.RepoID == binding.RepoID && marker.BaseURL == binding.BaseURL:
74					hosted.SyncedBranches = append(hosted.SyncedBranches, branch)
75				}
76			}
77			if len(broken) > 0 {
78				warning = fmt.Sprintf("hosted sync marker unreadable for branch(es) %s: %v", strings.Join(broken, ", "), brokenErr)
79			}
80		}
81		hosted.NoEgress = base.BrainNoEgressMode()
82		hosted.State = hosted.RepoState

90	// cause and remedy live in the verbose line (hostedStatusLine).
91	func hostedStateLabel(state string) string {
92		switch state {
93		case hostedStateConnected:
94			return "connected"
95		case hostedStateDisconnected:
96			return "disconnected"
97		default:
98			return "local-only"
99		}
100	}
101	
102	// hostedStatusLine is the verbose report's one-line hosted state: the label
103	// plus the cause or remedy. Coordinates are machine detail and stay in --json.
104	func hostedStatusLine(h *brainStatusHosted) string {
105		switch h.State {
106		case hostedStateConnected:
107			if n := len(h.SyncedBranches); n > 0 {
108				word := "branches"
109				if n == 1 {
110					word = "branch"
111				}
112				return fmt.Sprintf("Connected to Brainstore (%d %s synced)", n, word)
113			}
114			return "Connected to Brainstore (no branches synced yet)"
115		case hostedStateDisconnected:
116			return "Disconnected from Brainstore (run '" + base.BrainInvocation(os.LookupEnv, "connect") + "' to join)"
117		default:
118			// Local-only: name the variable actually set, and keep the underlying
119			// repo state visible so unsetting the variable is predictable.
120			return fmt.Sprintf("Local-only (%s set — unset it to resume; repo is %s)",
121				base.NoEgressToggleName(), hostedStateLabel(h.RepoState))
122		}
123	}

// hostedFake is an in-memory brainstore speaking the per-fact wire:
// POST …/brain/facts (identity-verified NDJSON batch, counts reply)
// and GET …/brain/facts (insert-ordered keyset feed, index page tokens,
// empty page terminal). Upserted records join the feed with the caller's
// server-stamped attribution, like the real store.
type hostedFake struct {
	mu           sync.Mutex
	items        []factsync.FeedItem
	index        map[string]int
	requests     int
	upsertCalls  int
	feedTokens   []string
	denyPush     bool // upsert → 403, the push-grant-denied shape
	denyFeed     bool // feed GET → 500, the pull-outage shape
	rejectTokens int  // while >0, any request with a pageToken → 400 once each
	callerBy     string
	callerHandle string
}

content.text:
COR-2279 client fix is implemented and fully green. Not committed yet — say the word and I'll commit and open the PR.

**What changed**

- `factsync`: 403 on `UpsertFacts`/`FactsFeedPage` now returns a wrapped `ErrNoAccess` sentinel (401 stays a plain error so auth breaks keep reaching the monitor).
- `hostedFactsSyncAndPull`: on a **pull** 403 it re-resolves placement once via `entire repo view`; if the origin maps to a different repo id in the **same cell** (deleted + re-onboarded), it rebinds and retries once; otherwise it records `no_access_until` (now + 24h) in `hosted.json` and prints one actionable line naming `entire brain connect`.
- While paused, all triggers skip silently: the sync gate, the push hint (before claiming its throttle), and therefore session-end and the daemon tick for every branch. `entire brain status` reports the pause; `connect` clears it by writing a fresh binding.
- All binding writes go through a new `brainstore.MutateHostedRepoBinding` — a locked read-modify-write that re-checks opt-out/repo id (a concurrent disconnect wins) and never creates or repairs an absent/unreadable `hosted.json`.

**Two deliberate deviations from the issue's proposal**

- The issue said "on ErrNoAccess skip the pull." I key the pause off the **pull** 403 instead: a push-only 403 is a real read-only-grant state (the COR-2030 staging smoke hit exactly push-403/pull-200) and must keep pulling. All four stuck bindings 403 on the pull, so they're all covered.
- Rebind requires the resolved cell URL to match the bound one, so an explicit `--repo-id/--api-url` binding (staging, non-default cell) is never silently retargeted to prod placement.

**Validation**

- New tests: pause + silent skip + expiry, rebind, cross-cell refusal, rebound-repo-still-denied, push-hint skip, `MutateHostedRepoBinding` invariants, `ErrNoAccess` wire behavior; extended the pull-only test to assert a push-only 403 never pauses.
- Full `./internal/cli` suite (231s), `factsync`, `brainstore`, `connect` packages, repo-wide `gofmt -l -s`, and `go vet ./...` all pass.
- Recorded the design decision as a Brain memory.

The monitor follow-up (rate-based alert) and the Kedaar-NR grant audit are server-side and stay on the issue.

content.content:
entire trail — Manage trails across repositories and branches A trail captures project intent across repositories and branches. Manage intent and discussions on the whole trail; use --repo and --branch to select context for checkout, sessions, findings, and approvals. When to use this: Trail commands talk to entire.io and read the saved login from the OS keyring (the Keychain on macOS), so they need network and keyring access. If you run commands in a sandbox, request unsandboxed execution for `entire trail` up front. input.command:
entire trail create --type bug --title "brain: stop hosted facts sync retrying 403 forever on a stale repo binding" --body "Client-side fix for COR-2279. The repo binding written by 'entire brain connect' never refreshed, so once the bound repo was deleted or the caller lost access, every trigger (session-end hook, daemon tick, push hint) retried the same 403 indefinitely — 11 denials in 10 minutes tripped brainstore's auth-failure monitor.

## What changed

- factsync surfaces 403 as an ErrNoAccess sentinel on both wire calls (401 unchanged, so auth-plumbing breaks still reach the monitor).
- On a pull 403, the sync re-resolves placement once via 'entire repo view'. A different repo id in the same cell (deleted and re-onboarded) rebinds and retries; otherwise the binding records a 24h no-access pause ('no_access_until' in hosted.json) and prints one line naming 'entire brain connect'.
- While paused, all background triggers skip silently, including the push hint before it claims its throttle. 'entire brain status' reports the pause. connect clears it by writing a fresh binding.
- All binding writes on this path go through a new locked read-modify-write (brainstore.MutateHostedRepoBinding) that re-checks opt-out and repo id, and never creates or repairs an absent or unreadable hosted.json.

## Deliberate deviations from the issue

- The pause keys off the pull 403, not any 403: a push-only denial is a real read-only-grant state (push 403, pull 200 — the COR-2030 staging smoke) and must keep pulling. All four stuck bindings 403 on the pull.
- Rebind requires the resolved cell URL to match the bound one, so an explicit --repo-id/--api-url binding (staging, non-default cell) is never silently retargeted.

## Validation

Full ./internal/cli suite, factsync, brainstore, and connect packages pass; gofmt -s and go vet clean. New tests cover pause, silent skip and expiry, rebind, cross-cell refusal, rebound-repo-still-denied, push-hint skip, Mutate invariants, and the ErrNoAccess wire behavior.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/evisdrenova/.claude/plugins/cache/entire-skills/entire/0.7.2/skills/address-findings

# Address Findings

Fix and resolve the open review findings on an Entire trail. A finding is a
review comment posted to a trail on entire.io: it has a file/line location, a
body, a severity, and sometimes a suggested unified-diff patch. This skill
fetches the open findings, applies or hand-fixes each one in the current
worktree, and marks it resolved on the trail.

## When to use / not use

Use when the user points at a trail — a URL like
`https://<host>/<forge>/<owner>/<repo>/trails/<number>/<slug>`, or a bare trail
number or branch — and asks to **address / fix / resolve** its findings or
review comments.

Do **not** use this skill for:

- A code review of the current diff — that is the `review` skill (read-only).
- Creating new findings — use `entire trail finding add`.

## Response Format

Begin the first response to this skill invocation with the line:

`Entire Address Findings:`

followed by a blank line, then the content. Apply the header to the **first
response only**. Omit it on error / early-exit responses (CLI missing, not
authenticated, trail not found, branch mismatch, no open findings).

## Rules

1. Make the smallest correct change that addresses each finding. Do not expand scope.
2. Only mark a finding resolved when you actually addressed it. If a finding is
   ambiguous or needs a human decision, leave it open and report it.
3. Do not commit or push. Leave changes in the working tree for the user to review.
4. Never weaken a test or assertion just to clear a finding.

## Process

### 1. Verify the CLI

Run `entire version`. If the command is not found, stop and tell the user:
"The Entire CLI is required but not installed. Install it from
https://entire.io/docs/cli and try again."

### 2. Resolve the trail selector

- If the argument is a trail URL, take the number from the `/trails/<number>/`
  path segment and use that number.
- If it is a bare trail number, id, or branch name, use it as-is.
- If you cannot determine a trail, stop and ask the user for the trail URL or number.

Use this value as the `<trail>` selector for every command below. `entire trail`
accepts a trail number, id, or branch name interchangeably, so no number lookup
is needed — a branch name works directly.

### 3. Fetch open findings

```bash
entire trail finding list <trail> --json --status open
```

- If the output reports that authentication is required, stop and tell the user:
  "`entire trail finding list` requires authentication. Run `entire login` and try again."
- If the `trail finding` subcommand is unavailable, or the API reports the
  feature is not enabled, stop and tell the user that trail findings may not be
  enabled for this account or repository. Do not invent findings.
- Parse the JSON. Each finding has an id, a severity, a status, a body, a
  location (file path + line range), and may include a suggested change (a
  unified diff).
- If there are no open findings, report "No open findings on this trail." and stop.

### 4. Branch guard (you must be on the trail's branch)

`entire trail finding apply` edits the local worktree, so you must be on the
trail's branch before changing files.

```bash
git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD                # current branch
entire trail list --json --status any -n 200   # locate the trail's branch
```

Find the trail whose `number` or `branch` matches your selector and read its `branch`.

- If the trail's branch differs from the current branch, stop and tell the user:
  "Trail `<trail>` targets branch `<trail-branch>`, but you are on
  `<current-branch>`. Check it out first (`entire trail checkout <trail>`) and
  re-run." Do not edit files.
- If you cannot find the trail in the list (e.g. pagination), do not hard-fail:
  warn that you could not verify the branch, and ask the user to confirm they are
  on the trail's branch before you continue.

### 5. Address each finding

Process findings highest severity first (high → medium → low). For each:

1. **If it has a suggested unified-diff change**, dry-run it first:

   ```bash
   entire trail finding apply <trail> <finding-id> --check
   ```

   If it applies cleanly, apply and resolve in one step:

   ```bash
   entire trail finding apply <trail> <finding-id> --resolve
   ```

2. **Otherwise** (no patch, the patch conflicts, or the fix needs reasoning):
   read the finding body, open the file at its location, and make the smallest
   correct edit that addresses it. If a fast, relevant local check exists for the
   touched code (a build or a focused test), run it. Then resolve:

   ```bash
   entire trail finding resolve <trail> <finding-id> -m "<one line: what you changed>"
   ```

3. **If you cannot confidently address it** (ambiguous, needs a product/design
   decision, or out of scope): leave it open, do not resolve it, and record it
   for the report.

### 6. Report

Summarize:

- Resolved via suggested patch — list finding ids and files.
- Resolved via manual edit — list finding ids, files, and a one-line of what changed.
- Left open for your decision — list finding ids and why.
- Any errors encountered.

Remind the user the changes are uncommitted and ready for review.

## Failure modes

- **CLI not installed** → install message (step 1).
- **Not authenticated** → "`entire trail finding list` requires authentication. Run `entire login` and try again."
- **Trail findings not enabled / API error** → tell the user the feature may be
  unavailable; do not fabricate findings.
- **Trail not found** → tell the user to check the URL or number; suggest
  `entire trail list --status any`.
- **Wrong branch** → stop with the checkout instruction (step 4).
- **Patch does not apply** → fall back to a manual edit; if you cannot fix it
  confidently, leave the finding open and report it.
- **Not a git repository** → stop and tell the user to run from inside the trail's repo.

input.command:
entire trail update entire-brain/444 --body "Client-side fix for COR-2279. The repo binding written by 'entire brain connect' never refreshed, so once the bound repo was deleted or the caller lost access, every trigger (session-end hook, daemon tick, push hint) retried the same 403 indefinitely — 11 denials in 10 minutes tripped brainstore's auth-failure monitor.

## What changed

- factsync surfaces 403 as an ErrNoAccess sentinel on both wire calls (401 unchanged, so auth-plumbing breaks still reach the monitor).
- On a pull 403, the sync re-resolves placement once via 'entire repo view'. A different repo id in the same cell (deleted and re-onboarded) rebinds and retries; otherwise the binding records a 24h no-access pause ('no_access_until' in hosted.json) and prints one line naming 'entire brain connect'. The paused line prints only when the pause was actually recorded; a write declined by a concurrent connect/disconnect is silent.
- While paused, all background triggers skip silently, including the push hint before it claims its throttle. 'entire brain status' reports the pause. connect clears it by writing a fresh binding.
- All binding writes on this path go through a new locked read-modify-write (brainstore.MutateHostedRepoBinding) that re-checks opt-out and repo id, and never creates or repairs an absent or unreadable hosted.json.

## Deliberate deviations from the issue

- The pause keys off the pull 403, not any 403: a push-only denial is a real read-only-grant state (push 403, pull 200 — the COR-2030 staging smoke) and must keep pulling. All four stuck bindings 403 on the pull.
- Rebind requires the resolved cell URL to match the bound one, so an explicit --repo-id/--api-url binding (staging, non-default cell) is never silently retargeted.

## Validation

Full ./internal/cli suite, factsync, brainstore, and connect packages pass; gofmt -s and go vet clean. New tests cover pause, silent skip and expiry, rebind, cross-cell refusal, rebound-repo-still-denied, push-hint skip, Mutate invariants, the ErrNoAccess wire behavior, and the declined-pause silence. All review findings addressed and resolved.
